q: The layer of the atmosphere that contains about 75% of its mass and in which nearly all living things and human activity occur is the _____
e: The layer of the atmosphere that contains about 75% of its mass and in which nearly all living things and human activity occur is the troposphere. The troposphere is the lowest layer, where almost all weather and living things are. Stratosphere would fill a different blank than troposphere.

q: Dry air contains approximately _____ nitrogen by volume.
e: Dry air contains approximately 78% nitrogen by volume. 78% is the idea that completes this fact. 21% would fill a different blank than 78%.

q: The concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere has increased from _____ to its present value of 0.04%.
e: The concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere has increased from 0.03% to its present value of 0.04%. 0.03% is the idea that completes this fact. 0.05% would fill a different blank than 0.03%.

q: Oxygen is the reactive part of the air and is involved in all of the following EXCEPT _____
e: Oxygen is the reactive part of the air and is involved in all of the following EXCEPT photosynthesis. Photosynthesis uses chlorophyll to trap light and build sugar from carbon dioxide and water. Respiration would fill a different blank than photosynthesis.

q: In the process of respiration, glucose reacts with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide, water, and _____
e: In the process of respiration, glucose reacts with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide, water, and energy. Your body uses oxygen from air with food to release energy. ATP would fill a different blank than energy.

q: Green plants need carbon dioxide for _____
e: Green plants need carbon dioxide for photosynthesis. Photosynthesis uses chlorophyll to trap light and build sugar from carbon dioxide and water. Respiration would fill a different blank than photosynthesis.

q: During fractional distillation of liquid air, the gas that boils off first is _____
e: During fractional distillation of liquid air, the gas that boils off first is nitrogen. Nitrogen is the idea that completes this fact. Oxygen would fill a different blank than nitrogen.

q: In the fractional distillation of air, water vapour and carbon dioxide are removed early because they would otherwise _____
e: In the fractional distillation of air, water vapour and carbon dioxide are removed early because they would otherwise freeze and block the pipes. Freeze and block the pipes is the idea that completes this fact. Form acids would fill a different blank than freeze and block the pipes.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the six main air pollutants listed in the textbook?
e: Carbon dioxide is the option that does not belong with the rest. Carbon dioxide is the idea that completes this fact. Carbon monoxide is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: Carbon monoxide is dangerous because it _____
a: reacts with haemoglobin and prevents oxygen transport
e: Carbon monoxide is dangerous because it reacts with haemoglobin and prevents oxygen transport. Oxygen supports respiration and combustion, and it is a very reactive non-metal. Causes acid rain would fill a different blank than reacts with haemoglobin and prevents oxygen transport.

q: Sulphur dioxide contributes to _____
e: Sulphur dioxide contributes to acid rain. Acid rain forms when sulfur and nitrogen oxides make acidic solutions in rain. Global warming would fill a different blank than acid rain.

q: Methane is considered a greenhouse gas because it _____
e: Methane is considered a greenhouse gas because it traps heat in the atmosphere. The atmosphere is the layer of air around Earth, split into troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, and thermosphere. Depletes the ozone layer would fill a different blank than traps heat in the atmosphere.

q: Ground-level ozone is formed by the reaction of nitrogen oxides with _____ in the presence of sunlight.
e: Ground-level ozone is formed by the reaction of nitrogen oxides with unburnt hydrocarbons in the presence of sunlight. A hydrocarbon contains only hydrogen and carbon. Sulphur dioxide would fill a different blank than unburnt hydrocarbons.

q: The greenhouse effect refers to the trapping of _____ by gases like carbon dioxide and methane.
e: The greenhouse effect refers to the trapping of infrared radiation by gases like carbon dioxide and methane. Infrared radiation is the idea that completes this fact. Ultraviolet radiation would fill a different blank than infrared radiation.

q: Which of the following is a natural source of methane?
e: Bacterial decay of vegetable matter is a natural source of methane. Bacterial decay of vegetable matter is the idea that completes this fact. Volcanic eruptions is not a natural source of methane.

q: Acid rain is defined as rain water with a pH less than _____
e: Acid rain is defined as rain water with a pH less than 5.0. 5.0 is the idea that completes this fact. 5.7 would fill a different blank than 5.0.

q: Naturally slightly acidic rain (pH ≈ 5.7) is due to carbon dioxide forming _____
e: Naturally slightly acidic rain (pH ≈ 5.7) is due to carbon dioxide forming carbonic acid. Carbonic acid is the idea that completes this fact. Nitric acid would fill a different blank than carbonic acid.

q: The chemical reaction $2SO_2(g) + O_2(g) + 2H_2O(l) \rightarrow 2H_2SO_4(aq)$ represents the formation of _____
e: The chemical reaction 2SO2(g) + O2(g) + 2H2O(l) to 2H2SO4(aq) represents the formation of sulphuric acid. Sulphuric acid is the idea that completes this fact. Nitric acid would fill a different blank than sulphuric acid.

q: Liquid nitrogen is used to _____
e: Liquid nitrogen is used to quick-freeze food. Quick-freeze food is the idea that completes this fact. Produce oxyacetylene flames would fill a different blank than quick-freeze food.

q: Helium is used to fill balloons because it is very light and _____
e: Helium is used to fill balloons because it is very light and inert. Inert is the idea that completes this fact. Dense would fill a different blank than inert.

q: Of all the water on Earth, the percentage that is fresh water is _____
e: Of all the water on Earth, the percentage that is fresh water is 2.5%. 2.5% is the idea that completes this fact. 0.02% would fill a different blank than 2.5%.

q: The purest form of natural water is _____
e: The purest form of natural water is rain water. Rain water is the idea that completes this fact. Sea water would fill a different blank than rain water.

q: Sea water contains approximately _____ soluble salts.
e: Sea water contains approximately 3.5% soluble salts. 3.5% is the idea that completes this fact. 2.5% would fill a different blank than 3.5%.

q: Water reaches its maximum density at approximately _____
e: Water reaches its maximum density at approximately 4°C. 4°C is the idea that completes this fact. 100°C would fill a different blank than 4°C.

q: Water is regarded as the most universal solvent because it dissolves _____
a: almost all substances to some extent
e: Water is regarded as the most universal solvent because it dissolves almost all substances to some extent. Almost all substances to some extent is the idea that completes this fact. Only ionic compounds would fill a different blank than almost all substances to some extent.

q: Temporary hardness of water is caused by dissolved _____
e: Temporary hardness of water is caused by dissolved calcium hydrogen carbonate. Hydrogen is the lightest element and a common fuel and reducing agent in the lab. Calcium sulphate would fill a different blank than calcium hydrogen carbonate.

q: Permanent hardness is caused by dissolved calcium or magnesium _____
e: Permanent hardness is caused by dissolved calcium or magnesium chlorides and sulphates. Chlorides and sulphates is the idea that completes this fact. Nitrates would fill a different blank than chlorides and sulphates.

q: When soap is added to hard water, it forms an insoluble white precipitate known as _____
e: When soap is added to hard water, it forms an insoluble white precipitate known as scum. Scum is the idea that completes this fact. Sludge would fill a different blank than scum.

q: The degree of hardness of water is expressed in terms of parts per million of _____ equivalent.
e: The degree of hardness of water is expressed in terms of parts per million of CaCO₃ equivalent. CaCO₃ is the idea that completes this fact. MgCl₂ would fill a different blank than CaCO₃.

q: Water with a hardness of 150 ppm is classified as _____
e: Water with a hardness of 150 ppm is classified as hard. Hard water has a lot of calcium and magnesium ions, so soap does not lather well. Moderately hard would fill a different blank than hard.

q: Boiling removes _____ hardness from water.
e: Boiling removes temporary hardness from water. Temporary is the idea that completes this fact. Both types of would fill a different blank than temporary.

q: Washing soda softens hard water by precipitating calcium ions as _____
e: Washing soda softens hard water by precipitating calcium ions as calcium carbonate. Calcium carbonate is the idea that completes this fact. Calcium sulphate would fill a different blank than calcium carbonate.

q: In the Permutit method, sodium ions in zeolite are replaced by _____ from hard water.
e: In the Permutit method, sodium ions in zeolite are replaced by Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions from hard water. Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions is the idea that completes this fact. H⁺ ions would fill a different blank than Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions.

q: A common source of water pollution that introduces heavy metals like Pb and Hg is _____
e: A common source of water pollution that introduces heavy metals like Pb and Hg is industrial waste. Industrial waste is the idea that completes this fact. Agricultural runoff would fill a different blank than industrial waste.

q: Chlorination in water treatment is primarily used to _____
e: Chlorination in water treatment is primarily used to kill microorganisms. Kill microorganisms is the idea that completes this fact. Remove suspended particles would fill a different blank than kill microorganisms.

q: Distillation produces pure water but is not used on a large scale because it is _____
e: Distillation produces pure water but is not used on a large scale because it is far too expensive. Far too expensive is the idea that completes this fact. Ineffective is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: Fluorination of water is done to _____
e: Fluorination of water is done to prevent tooth decay. Prevent tooth decay is the idea that completes this fact. Improve taste would fill a different blank than prevent tooth decay.

q: Detergents do not form scum in hard water because their calcium and magnesium salts are _____
e: Detergents do not form scum in hard water because their calcium and magnesium salts are soluble. Soluble is the idea that completes this fact. Insoluble is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: Limescale in kettles is mainly composed of _____
e: Limescale in kettles is mainly composed of CaCO₃. CaCO₃ is the idea that completes this fact. CaSO₄ would fill a different blank than CaCO₃.

q: The chemical equation $\text{Ca(HCO}_3)_2(aq) \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{CaCO}_3(s) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l) + \text{CO}_2(g)$ represents the removal of _____ hardness.
e: The chemical equation Ca(HCO3)2(aq) CaCO3(s) + H2O(l) + CO2(g) represents the removal of temporary hardness. Temporary is the idea that completes this fact. Permanent would fill a different blank than temporary.

q: The top layer of soil, rich in organic material and dark brown in colour, is called the _____
e: The top layer of soil, rich in organic material and dark brown in colour, is called the top soil. Top soil is the idea that completes this fact. Bedrock would fill a different blank than top soil.

q: The subsoil is lighter in colour than top soil because it contains _____
e: The subsoil is lighter in colour than top soil because it contains less humus. Less humus is the idea that completes this fact. No minerals would fill a different blank than less humus.

q: Bedrock, or parent rock, contains _____
e: Bedrock, or parent rock, contains no organic matter. No organic matter is the idea that completes this fact. High humus content would fill a different blank than no organic matter.

q: The mineral matter in soil makes up approximately _____ of its composition.
e: The mineral matter in soil makes up approximately 45% of its composition. 45% is the idea that completes this fact. 5% would fill a different blank than 45%.

q: Organic matter in soil accounts for about _____ of its total composition.
e: Organic matter in soil accounts for about 5% of its total composition. 5% is the idea that completes this fact. 20% would fill a different blank than 5%.

q: Soil texture is determined by the relative proportion of sand, silt, and _____
e: Soil texture is determined by the relative proportion of sand, silt, and clay. Clay is the idea that completes this fact. Humus would fill a different blank than clay.

q: Clay particles feel _____ when wet.
e: Clay particles feel heavy and sticky when wet. Heavy and sticky is the idea that completes this fact. Smooth would fill a different blank than heavy and sticky.

q: Sand particles are _____ compared to silt and clay.
e: Sand particles are the biggest compared to silt and clay. The biggest is the idea that completes this fact. Intermediate in size would fill a different blank than the biggest.

q: A soil with 30% clay, 50% sand, and 20% silt is classified as _____
e: A soil with 30% clay, 50% sand, and 20% silt is classified as sandy clay loam. Sandy clay loam is the idea that completes this fact. Silty clay would fill a different blank than sandy clay loam.

q: The essential macro-nutrients obtained from soil include nitrogen, phosphorus, and _____
e: The essential macro-nutrients obtained from soil include nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. Potassium is the idea that completes this fact. Calcium would fill a different blank than potassium.

q: Nitrogen is especially important for _____ growth in plants.
e: Nitrogen is especially important for leaf growth in plants. Leaf is the idea that completes this fact. Root would fill a different blank than leaf.

q: Phosphorus is particularly associated with the development of a strong _____ system.
e: Phosphorus is particularly associated with the development of a strong root system. Root is the idea that completes this fact. Leaf would fill a different blank than root.

q: Potassium plays a key role in the _____ balance in plants.
e: Potassium plays a key role in the water balance in plants. Water is the idea that completes this fact. Nutrient would fill a different blank than water.

q: Most plants grow best when the soil pH is between _____
e: Most plants grow best when the soil pH is between 5.5 and 7.0. 5.5 and 7.0 is the idea that completes this fact. 4.0 and 5.0 would fill a different blank than 5.5 and 7.0.

q: If soil is too acidic, it can be treated by adding _____
e: If soil is too acidic, it can be treated by adding lime. Lime is the idea that completes this fact. Fertilizer would fill a different blank than lime.

q: Alkaline soils (pH > 8.5) can be treated with _____
e: Alkaline soils (pH > 8.5) can be treated with gypsum. Gypsum is the idea that completes this fact. Lime would fill a different blank than gypsum.

q: Lead particulates from automobile exhausts settle on soil near _____
e: Lead particulates from automobile exhausts settle on soil near highways. Highways is the idea that completes this fact. Rivers would fill a different blank than highways.

q: Pesticides in soil undergo degradation through biodegradation, chemical degradation, and _____
e: Pesticides in soil undergo degradation through biodegradation, chemical degradation, and photochemical reactions. Photochemical reactions is the idea that completes this fact. Evaporation would fill a different blank than photochemical reactions.

q: Repeated or excessive use of the same fertiliser is a source of _____
e: Repeated or excessive use of the same fertiliser is a source of soil pollution. Soil pollution is the idea that completes this fact. Noise pollution would fill a different blank than soil pollution.

q: Soil filters water, provides nutrients to crops, and helps regulate the Earth’s _____
e: Soil filters water, provides nutrients to crops, and helps regulate the Earth’s temperature. Temperature is the idea that completes this fact. Rotation would fill a different blank than temperature.
